title: No Verified Pet-Theft Case: Demand Records, Protection, and Abolition
excerpt: No police seizure, court verdict, or intercepted shipment appears in current records. Public trust needs proof, protection for families, and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
No verified police seizure, court verdict, or intercepted shipment appears in current material. That leaves families without a documented case to examine—and leaves no honest basis for inventing cages, poison baits, stun guns, victims, or transport conditions.

Evidence before outrage

Pet theft, illegal transport, quarantine violations, and uninspected slaughter demand named agencies, dates, quantities, case numbers, and source records. Without those details, claims remain unverified. Anger belongs on proven criminal conduct and enforcement failures, not on Vietnamese identity, culture, or communities. Vietnamese families deserve protection for companion animals and transparent action against illicit operators.

Biosecurity cannot rely on assumptions

Rabies exposure generally occurs when infected saliva enters bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. Household exposure incidents and commercial supply chains remain separate questions; neither permits unsupported causal claims. See WHO rabies guidance.

Demand records. Demand reform.

SDE calls for nationwide abolition by 2030, stronger veterinary controls, and protection for stolen companions. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action, then follow campaign updates reaching decision-makers.
